messages:
maya (AE): Hey team — Strategic acct wants vendor risk pack for procurement. Their security asked specifically for: data residency guarantees, a data flow diagram, and a list of subprocessors. They also want confirmation we don’t persist raw customer prompts in logs. Can we assemble and turn around by EOD tomorrow?

dmitri (SE): Do they have any special residency region? EU-only or multi-region? Also: is this for hosted API or Dedicated/Private?

maya (AE): EU-only for production traffic, but dev/test can be US. It's for Hosted API.

anita (Security): We can provide a data flow diagram (high-level) + subprocessors list. Quick facts to include: at-rest encryption (AES-256), in-transit TLS1.2+, customer-configurable KMS for Dedicated/Private, and retention policy for logs. For Hosted: prompt/response metadata is logged for observability by default; we can redact or disable storage on a customer basis per contract.

Sidenote: SIG/CAIQ answers needed? They mentioned a vendor risk portal that wants SIG v12 + SC access. We have a filled CAIQ template but a couple of control narratives need updates for regional handling.

sophie (Legal): If they're EU-only, we should highlight subprocessors that could process data outside EU (e.g., CI/CD providers, analytics). We'll flag which subprocessors have EU data residency options. Also recommend adding a data processing addendum (DPA) and if they insist — SCCs.

dmitri (SE): I'll draft a DFD here — simple ASCII so they can see hops quickly, then attach a proper diagram.

vendor-risk-bot: Automated note — we maintain an internal register of subprocessors: AWS (eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west2) for compute, CloudStorageEdge (EU-only for backups), Sentry (error monitoring), Datadog (metrics), Auth0 (SSO), FastLog (logging pipeline). Full vendor list available on request.

anita (Security): Draft DFD (short):
```
[Client App] -> HTTPS -> [Redwood API Gateway (eu-west-1)]
  -> [Inference Cluster (gpus, eu-west-1)]
  -> [KV/Cache (redis) eu-west-1]
  -> [Optional: Async Logging -> FastLog (can be EU)]
  -> [Metrics -> Datadog (EU region option)]
  -> [Audit + Access Logs -> Encrypted Object Store (CloudStorageEdge, EU-only backup)]
Notes: Customer-owned keys (KMS) supported in Dedicated/Private. Hosted default: managed keys.
```

maya (AE): This is great. Can we call out where PII might be transiently present (prompts/responses) and our recommendations to avoid retention? The customer wants an explicit statement.

anita (Security): Yes — include this snippet: "By default, Hosted API may temporarily buffer request/response content in memory and for short-term operational logs (configurable). We provide options to: 1) disable request/response logging, 2) enable automatic redaction of fields via customer-supplied JSON schema, or 3) route logs to customer-managed storage via secure ingestion (recommended for regulated PII)." Add that we will not use customer data to train models.

sophie (Legal): Also note subprocessors with access to logs: FastLog and CloudStorageEdge if logging/backup enabled; Sentry has access to error traces (can be configured to strip payloads). Provide their EU data processing locations where available.

dmitri (SE): ETA to produce deliverables: 1) one-page DFD + bullet list of where PII may appear (by EOD today) 2) Subprocessor table with EU residency flags (tomorrow morning) 3) Updated CAIQ control narratives (48 hrs). Anyone blocking?

maya (AE): No blockers. Can you also add a short note about data residency enforcement — e.g., smart routing to eu-west-1, and fallback policy if eu capacity exhausted? Customer asked: will data ever leave EU?

anita (Security): For Hosted: policy is region-aware routing; we route to eu-west-1 for EU-tagged customers. In exceptional cases of failover we will attempt EU-region capacity first, then fall back to nearest compatible region if configured in contract. We'll provide a clear statement: "We do not replicate production inference data outside the EU unless explicit customer consent or emergency failover per contract." We'll also include audit trail capability for cross-region events.

sophie (Legal): I'll prep a redline for the DPA clause on data residency and subprocessors. If they require offline scans of CAIQ, request NDAs — vendor portal has the encrypted package flow.

maya (AE): Perfect. I'll update the buyer: expect DFD + high-level subprocessor list today, full subprocessor + CAIQ updates tomorrow. Thanks all :pray:

vendor-risk-bot: Reminder — attach current subprocessor CSV here when ready: /internal/vendor_register/subprocessors-current.csv (access-controlled).
